_comment: ADR 0003. The only place detection numbers live. Hot-reloaded on change. Floors were tuned 2026-08-11 against measured LABDEMO steady state (proc: Lab Router .08s, Cloud API .05s, EMR Source 0; queue wait: only Cloud API at .03s) -- the original 1.0s floors were 12-33x those baselines, so the floor bound instead of the multiplier and a 10x regression produced no finding at all.
_comment_info_severity: DELIBERATE: severity 'info' is unreachable for the seven per-host rules, and system_alert is the only source of an info finding. Each comparative rule's firing gate equals its severityBands.warning (e.g. queue_buildup fires at 5x and warns at 5x), so anything that fires is at least a warning; dead_host and stalled_host carry fixed severities. Do NOT 'fix' this by lowering a warning band -- that would require lowering the firing GATE, which widens what fires and reintroduces exactly the false positives MVP §6 names as the top risk. A quiet findings list is the point. Raised by Dev C on #8 after observing 46 live findings with no info among them.
_comment_sustained: TWO gates, both must pass. sustainedSamples guards a lone bad scrape; sustainedSeconds guards against a fast poll rate shortening the debounce below what MVP 6 intends (#44). Must be reachable within sustainedSamples polls WITH MARGIN, or it silently forces an extra one. Two values that failed at a 5s poll: 8 is unreachable in 2 samples and confirms on the 3rd (measured 12.8s debounce); 5 is reachable only by exact equality, and because the sample is stamped after a variable-duration fetch, any poll quicker than its predecessor slips confirmation to the 3rd sample -- intermittently 10.2s instead of 5.3s. 4 leaves 1000ms of slack at the shipping rate and still decouples the debounce from the poll rate at shorter intervals, which is the coupling this gate exists to break. Derivation in src/config/thresholds.ts, guards in test/engine.test.ts. AND IT SETS A FLOOR UNDER POLL_INTERVAL_MS, at the shipped 5000ms itself: the gate needs (sustainedSamples-1) x interval > sustainedSeconds x 1000, i.e. 1 x 5000 > 4000, so there is 1000ms of margin and 4500ms already breaks an invariant. Coverage is not the first thing to lose -- invariants fail at 4500 and 2500, finding types only at 1750 (#64, #65). Shortening the interval means retuning this number in the same change. Set sustainedSeconds to 0 for the old sample-only behaviour.
_comment_referenceBaselines: A STATED normal that does not move, overriding the rolling mean for the host+metric it names. Why one is needed: the rolling mean includes the samples judged against it, so a gradually RISING metric drags its own baseline up. For a linear ramp the closed form is 2n/(n+1) -- it approaches 2.0 and never crosses the 5.0 gate at any depth, any duration, and (because the slope cancels out of the algebra) any inflow rate. Measured live: the ratio pinned at exactly 2.00 while the queue climbed past 1200, and queue_buildup never fired. That is CLAUDE.md 5.1's self-inflation, but the RAMP case is worse than the step case documented there: a step fires for ~12 minutes then clears while the problem persists, whereas a ramp never fires at all. MVP 1 got away with it because its scenarios were steps (disable a host, break its target) and dead_host is absolute; MVP 2's scenario is a ramp on a host whose status stays OK, so nothing absolute backs it up. WHY 0 FOR Cloud API queued, and why 0 is legal here when no other number in this file may be: a healthy Cloud API genuinely holds no queue, so 0 is the true normal rather than a convenient one. The rule's own `baseline > 0 ? depth/baseline : INFINITY` branch then reduces the test to absoluteFloor (50), which is the correct reading -- any standing queue is abnormal, and the floor decides whether it is worth reporting. WHY NOT A MULTI-DAY WINDOW INSTEAD: it fixes the arithmetic but not the demo. A fresh compose up has no days of history, minBaselineSamples is satisfied after 12 samples, and a 3-day window holding only the last minute would claim evidence it does not have. A stated reference is the more honest artifact -- it says 'assumed', where a long window implies 'measured'. Absent for a host+metric, behaviour is exactly the rolling mean as before. A reference also skips the warm-up wait for the metric it covers, which is a side effect rather than a feature.
_comment_earlyWarning: MVP 2. Projects a rising metric forward to its threshold; see contracts/earlywarning-api.md. fitWindowSeconds 300 rather than the full baselineWindowSeconds: a least-squares fit over 1800s systematically UNDERSTATES a rise that started two minutes ago, which is exactly the case Early Warning exists to catch -- the older half of the window is flat and drags the slope toward zero. horizonSeconds equals baselineWindowSeconds deliberately: do not project further forward than the span of history the fit is grounded in, because a 90-minute ETA off a 5-minute fit is arithmetic rather than information. minFitSamples reuses minBaselineSamples (12) and is not independently chosen -- below 12 the baseline is null, so max(baseline x multiplier, absoluteFloor) has no baseline arm and there is no target to project toward; a projection with no threshold is meaningless rather than merely imprecise. REACHABILITY, the same invariant sustainedSeconds has: fitWindowSeconds / (POLL_INTERVAL_MS/1000) must exceed minFitSamples with margin. At the shipped 5000ms poll that is 60 samples available against 12 required, so 5x headroom, and first projection ~60s after engine start. Shortening fitWindowSeconds below 60s at that poll rate makes a projection structurally impossible and the module would go silent with no error -- the #64 failure mode in a new place.

hostOverrides._comment: Rare and always commented. Raising a bound to silence a nag also raises it for a genuine regression.

Cloud API._comment: Outbound operation: its latency includes a simulated remote call, so it tolerates more than the in-process hosts. 0.3s is ~6x its measured 0.05s.
